name: Wyndham Hotels & Resorts
headline: The world's largest budget hotel franchisor, collecting fees on 868,900 rooms with almost no capital.
what_short: Franchisor of budget and midscale hotels
what_it_does: Wyndham licenses 25 hotel brands to over 6,200 franchisees who own 8,389 hotels with 868,900 rooms, mostly in economy and midscale categories in smaller cities. A franchisee pays a royalty of about 5% of room revenue plus a 2% to 4% marketing and reservation fee, typically under long contracts. 77% of its royalty profit comes from the US.
why_it_passed: It collects fees on a huge room base and puts in very little capital itself: property and equipment is only $104 million.
It earned 36% to 67% a year before tax on its tangible capital from 2021 to 2025, close to the best kind of business, which needs almost no money put in to grow.
Revenue is tied to rooms, room revenue per available room, and fee rate, all of which the company reports every year.
The analysis found management honest, and the franchise system still stands against three larger rivals.
why_not_now: The analysis values the shares at $34.94 to $42.59 against a price of $73.42, well above the top of the range. A buyer at that price would expect only about 4.0% to 4.7% a year, below a 30-year US Treasury bond (5.56%).
watch: It has lost ground to all three rivals the analysis compared it with, and it pays owners to sign (development advances of $343 million at the end of 2025) to keep winning rooms.
Debt is $2.7 billion, rated Ba1 / BB+, with about 95% of the term loan swapped to fixed rates and those swaps expiring in 2027 and 2028.
Online booking sites, AI assistants and alternative lodging are named threats, and a $160 million charge related to its Revo acquisition cut 2025 returns.
